newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan firms to follow TEPCO power rate cut.
newsitem.headline: More Japan firms to follow TEPCO power rate cut.

text.p: Three Japanese electric power utilities said on Monday they planned to cut rates next year, following Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc's (TEPCO) announcement on Friday that it would cut rates in early 1998.
The three firms are Tohoku Electric Power Co Inc, Hokkaido Electric Power Co Inc and Okinawa Electric Power Co Ltd.

Tohoku and Hokkaido Electric, which serve northern Japan, said they plan to cut their rates early next year, while Okinawa Electric, which serves Japan's southern island of Okinawa, said it would lower prices by the end of next year.
TEPCO, Japan's largest power utility, said on Friday it would cut rates early next year in response to mounting pressure from the public and private sectors to lower electricity rates.
Japan's 10 utilities have all made clear their intention to cut rates.
But three of the utilities, Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, Chubu Electric Power Co Inc and Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc, have yet to make clear a time schedule.

Shortly after TEPCO's announcement on Friday, Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc and Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc said they planned to cut their rates early next year, while Shikoku Electric Power Co Inc said it may lower rates next year.
None of the firms, including TEPCO, has indicated by how much their rates would be cut.
Last year, the Japanese government said it would aim to bring Japan's electricity rates into line with international levels by 2001 as part of a wider economic reform programme.

Industry estimates indicate that the average family in Japan pays about 20 percent more for its electricity than a German family and 30 percent more than a family in the United States. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
